question: Does each of the 39 registered decimal-primer survivors admit globally consistent, independent bijective plaintext and ciphertext alphabets for all 24 aligned crib equations?
model: c(C_i)-p(P_i)=k[i] modulo 26 with independently unknown bijective alphabets, a recurrence-expanded decimal primer, and all 24 aligned cribs

domain.primers: the exact 39 sorted survivors in PRIMERS-0001 run-002
domain.component_root: alphabetically lowest plaintext symbol at relative coordinate zero
domain.global_symmetry: first sorted component fixed at offset zero
domain.unconstrained_letters: placed alphabetically in unused alphabet slots

search: derive exact bipartite graph coordinates, reject local contradictions, sort components by decreasing constrained size, then exhaustively backtrack over component offsets with plaintext and ciphertext bit masks
evaluation_unit: candidate component offsets across all 39 primers; Python verifier has an independent 1000000-state cap per primer
dependencies: Cargo.lock offline; Python standard library; no network or stochastic input
falsification_criterion: Any malformed component, alphabet, key, equation or primer fails verification; any Rust/Python decision disagreement fails; any budget-exhausted decision leaves the milestone unresolved.
limitations: A feasible witness proves compatibility with arbitrary independent alphabets, not the historical alphabets or intended plaintext.
The model uses only the registered 24 aligned crib letters and the declared primer recurrence.
The Python implementation is an independent algorithm written by the same project coordinator, not a fresh-context external review.
